findings.title: Optimized paginator crashes on datetime audit logs
findings.body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint (organization_auditlogs.py around line 79) switches to OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime" when optimized_pagination=true. OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does int(math.floor/ceil) on the ordering field, and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor number. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so the first page with any rows raises TypeError inside build_cursor. A non-zero cursor then builds a WHERE clause comparing a timestamptz column to an integer and fails in SQL. The new path is untested and 500s for every admin who passes the flag; DateTimePaginator already implements the correct key conversion and was the previous paginator.

findings.title: Negative cursor offsets break pagination globally
findings.body: BasePaginator.get_result now does start_offset = max(0, offset) unless cursor.is_prev, and the comments claim negative offsets are safe because the queryset handles them. Django raises ValueError on any negative slice, so a previous-page cursor with a negative offset still 500s. A forward cursor with a negative offset is silently clamped to 0 while build_cursor still does next_offset = cursor.offset + limit using the original negative offset, so the next Link cursor skips or repeats rows. This is on every BasePaginator endpoint, not just the new class. OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result (line 877) goes further and, when enable_advanced_features is set, passes the client-supplied negative offset straight into queryset[start:stop], which 500s. That flag is turned on for audit-log superusers/global-access members via a query param. Client-controlled cursors must keep rejecting negative offsets instead of clamping or slicing with them.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE sums scores and evicts the wrong spans
findings.body: The merge from sets to sorted sets uses ZUNIONSTORE with the default AGGREGATE SUM (lines 47 and 53). Span payloads are the members and end_timestamp_precise is the score. On Kafka redelivery, or any merge where the same payload is already in both keys, the scores are added. Later zpopmin (line 63) keeps the highest scores, so redelivered spans look newer than they are and genuinely newer spans are dropped once the segment exceeds 1000. Unions should use AGGREGATE MAX (or otherwise preserve the original timestamp) so eviction order stays the end timestamp.

findings.title: In-place SET to ZSET change will WRONGTYPE on rollout
findings.body: Segment keys stay span-buf:s:{project:trace}:span_id, but process_spans now ZADDs and the Lua script uses ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZPOPMIN, while flush uses ZSCAN. Existing keys are Redis SETs. During a rolling deploy, old consumers SADD/SUNIONSTORE/SSCAN and new consumers ZADD/ZSCAN on the same keys, and both get WRONGTYPE. Batches fail, segments already buffered cannot be flushed or merged, and keys sit until TTL. Ship a new key prefix or an explicit migration; do not reinterpret live SET keys as ZSETs.

findings.title: Flush no longer enforces max_segment_spans
findings.body: The incremental ZSCAN loader used to stop and drop a segment once it passed max_segment_spans (default 1001). That guard is gone, and the new cap is a hardcoded 1000 inside add-buffer.lua, not self.max_segment_spans, and it is not passed into the script. ZADD runs in a separate pipeline before the Lua eviction, and the flusher can run concurrently with workers, so a flush can observe a segment before zpopmin. The flusher will now load and produce the entire segment, which can OOM the consumer on a large trace. The byte-size check does not replace a span-count ceiling. Eviction also uses zpopmin with no exception for the segment/root span, so a root whose end_timestamp_precise is not in the top 1000 scores is deleted and the segment is flushed without a segment span. Restore a flush-time cap wired to max_segment_spans, and do not evict the root span.

findings.title: Redirect walk cap lowered and still writes a partial redirect
findings.body: The parent-redirect walk used to stop at 10000 with a comment that deeper segment trees would not be joined correctly. It now stops at 1000 and, on exhaustion, still HSETs span_id to whatever intermediate set_span_id it landed on and continues the merge. A chain or cycle longer than 1000 hops is silently attached to the wrong segment instead of being left unjoined or failed. If the cap is only a Redis-latency bound, the script should not persist a truncated redirect.

findings.title: No test for insert-time eviction or score-preserving merges
findings.body: Existing buffer tests only insert a handful of spans that share one timestamp and then sort flushed output by span_id. Nothing covers a segment larger than 1000, which scores zpopmin keeps, whether the root/segment span survives eviction, ZUNIONSTORE score behavior on redelivery, or flush of a segment that exceeds max_segment_spans. Those are the behaviors this change adds, and the current assertions would still pass if eviction dropped the wrong spans or the cap never ran.
